I have everything I need from both sources. Here's your schedule.

## Sources used

| Source | What I took from it |
|---|---|
| UMN Extension, **"Upper Midwest home garden care schedule"** (reviewed 2026) | Month-range timings for all planting + maintenance tasks, including the dual windows |
| UMN Extension, **"Planting the vegetable garden"** | Crop-by-crop outdoor dates, indoor seed-starting dates, cool/warm/tender definitions, soil-temperature thresholds |
| **USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map** (planthardiness.ars.usda.gov) | Assessed for suitability — see caveat below |

---

## First, the USDA map caveat — read this before the table

You were right to flag it. The USDA map is an **interactive Esri web application**, not a page of text. It works by ZIP-code lookup or by clicking the map, and returns a zone band. Two things follow:

**It cannot give you a number here.** You didn't give me a ZIP code or town, so I did not retrieve a zone for you, and I'm not going to invent one. Run your own ZIP through the lookup at planthardiness.ars.usda.gov to get it.

**More importantly, even once you have your zone, it will not date a single row in the table below.** USDA zones are derived from the *average annual extreme minimum winter temperature*, in 10 °F bands split into 5 °F half-zones. That statistic answers one question: will a perennial, shrub or tree survive my winter? It does **not** encode last spring frost date, first fall frost date, growing-season length, or soil warm-up rate — which are precisely the variables that drive every date in an annual vegetable calendar. Two locations can share a zone and have last-frost dates weeks apart.

So the map is the right tool for the *perennials, rhubarb, asparagus and spring bulbs* on your list, and the wrong tool for the *vegetable timings*. For those, UMN's own page tells you what to use instead: **soil temperature is the determinant**, read via a soil thermometer or the Minnesota Department of Agriculture's Six-Inch Soil Temperature Network. Cool-season crops go in at 40–50 °F soil; warm-season at 50–60 °F.

The reference frost date underlying the calendar below is UMN's **"last frost, mid-to-late May."**

---

## Month-by-month schedule

Where Extension gives two windows, both are kept, with its "best time" label preserved.

| Month | Planting / sowing | Seasonal maintenance |
|---|---|---|
| **Jan** | *(nothing outdoors)* | Plan beds; order seed; get soil tested |
| **Feb** | **Indoors:** early Feb onion (transplants); mid-Feb celery | — |
| **Mar** | Direct seed spring cover crops (peas, oats, clover) **as soon as ground thaws**. **Indoors** (mid-Mar → early May window opens): early Mar broccoli, brussels sprouts, early cabbage, cauliflower, head lettuce; mid-Mar eggplant, okra, pepper | **Cut back perennials (Mar–Apr)** |
| **Apr** | Cool-season veg direct seed/transplant, April. Early–mid Apr: early cabbage. Mid-Apr: asparagus crowns, broccoli, brussels sprouts, collards, cauliflower, endive, horseradish, head lettuce, onion (seed/transplant/sets), parsley, rhubarb, spinach. Mid-Apr→early May: peas. Mid-Apr→mid-May: potatoes, radish. Mid-Apr→early Jun: carrots. Mid-Apr→mid-Jun: beets, kohlrabi, leaf lettuce. Mid-Apr→early Jul: kale. Last week Apr: moderately cold-tolerant crops (carrots, beets, potatoes). **Indoors:** early Apr tomato; mid-Apr late cabbage, sweet potato roots | **Divide perennials — window 1 opens: 2nd wk Apr → 3rd wk Jun (best time)**. **Watering season begins: 3rd wk Apr → end Nov** |
| **May** | Early May: Swiss chard, parsnips. Early May→early Jun: cucumbers. **Frost gate: mid-to-late May, or first week of June** — heat-loving crops (sweet corn, beans, tomatoes, peppers). Mid-May: dry shell beans, celery, muskmelon, pumpkin, summer + winter squash, tomatoes, watermelon. Mid-May→early Jun: lima beans, rutabaga. Mid-May→mid-Jun: sweet corn. Mid-May→early Jul: snap beans. Last wk May→2nd wk Jun: summer bulbs. Last wk May→end Jun: direct seed summer veg. **Annuals — window 1: last wk May → end Jun (best time)**. Perennials: last wk May→Aug | **Mulch beds — window 1: May → end Jun (best time)**. **Weed control: May–Sep.** **Fertilize: last wk May–Aug** |
| **Jun** | Early Jun: broccoli, brussels sprouts, late cabbage, cauliflower, eggplant, pepper, sweet potato roots | **Deadhead: Jun–Sep.** Divide perennials best window closes 3rd wk Jun; **window 2 opens: end Jun → end Aug**. Mulch best window closes end Jun |
| **Jul** | Early Jul: Chinese cabbage. **Second sowing window opens — mid-Jul: fall vegetables (carrots, beets, broccoli)**. **Annuals — window 2: Jul → end Aug** | Divide bearded iris: late Jul–early Aug |
| **Aug** | Fall sowing continues **through mid-Aug (spinach, lettuce)**. Early Aug: kohlrabi, leaf lettuce, radish, spinach, turnip | Divide peonies: late Aug–Sep. Fertilize, perennial planting, annual planting and perennial division all close end Aug |
| **Sep** | Fall cover crops that winter-kill: Sep (peas, oats). Fall cover crops: Sep–Oct (ryegrass, rye, rapeseed, oats, winter wheat, winter rye). **Spring bulbs: 2nd wk Sep → mid-Nov** | Divide peonies through Sep. Weed control and deadheading close end Sep |
| **Oct** | Overwintering cover crops: Oct (winter wheat, winter rye, hairy vetch). Spring bulbs continue | **Mulch beds — window 2: Oct → end Nov**. **Clean up vegetable garden: Oct–Nov.** Till in late fall to allow earlier spring planting |
| **Nov** | Spring bulbs through mid-Nov | **Cut back perennials (Nov)**. Watering, mulching and cleanup all close end Nov |
| **Dec** | — | Dormant; plan next season |

**The four true dual-window tasks**, kept intact as you asked: divide perennials (Apr–Jun *best* / late Jun–Aug), mulch beds (May–Jun *best* / Oct–Nov), plant annuals (late May–Jun *best* / Jul–Aug), and heat-loving vegetables (mid-late May *or* first week of June — here Extension offers two acceptable windows with no "best" label, so don't read a preference into it). Separately, leaf lettuce, radish and kohlrabi are explicitly sown **twice**: mid-April and again in August.

---

## What to buy or start ahead of each window

| Buy/start by | For which window |
|---|---|
| **Dec–Jan** | Soil test submitted; seed order placed; trays or 3–4″ peat pots, seed-starting mix (2 parts loam : 1 sand : 1 organic matter, or premixed), clear plastic covers, grow lights, fine-rose watering can, dibble |
| **Late Jan** | Onion seed — sowing early Feb |
| **Early Feb** | Celery seed — sowing mid-Feb |
| **Late Feb** | Broccoli, brussels sprouts, early cabbage, cauliflower, head lettuce seed — sowing early Mar |
| **Early Mar** | Eggplant, okra, pepper seed — sowing mid-Mar |
| **Late Mar** | Tomato seed (early Apr); soil thermometer; cover crop seed (peas/oats/clover); asparagus crowns, rhubarb, horseradish, onion sets — mid-Apr planting |
| **Early Apr** | Late cabbage seed + sweet potato slips; seed potatoes; pea, spinach, radish, carrot, beet, lettuce seed |
| **Late Apr** | Mulch material; summer bulbs; annual and perennial transplants; fertilizer per soil-test result; **hot caps** for cucumbers, pumpkins, watermelons — set over soil **one week before planting** |
| **Early May** | Warm-season transplants (tomato, pepper, eggplant) — begin hardening off; sweet corn and bean seed |
| **Late Jun** | Fall-crop seed: carrots, beets, broccoli for mid-Jul; spinach and lettuce for early–mid Aug |
| **Late Aug** | Cover crop seed for Sep–Oct; spring bulbs for the 2nd-wk-Sep window |
| **Late Sep** | Overwintering cover crop seed (winter wheat, winter rye, hairy vetch); second round of mulch |

Two things that cannot be transplanted and must be direct-seeded: **radishes, carrots and beets.** Warm-season crops are the reverse — they need a long season and **will not mature if seeded directly**, so tomatoes, peppers and eggplant must be bought or started indoors.
